newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold exchange volume up on low prices.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold exchange volume up on low prices.

text.p: Volume on the Istanbul gold exchange rose to 781 kilos on Monday from 689 on Friday as free market traders took advantage of worldwide low prices to replace stocks sold over the weekend, dealers said.
Gold fell in dollar terms to $376.10 an ounce from $377.75 on Friday, following European trends, but firmed slightly to 1,216,600 lira per gram from 1,216,000, due to the weak lira.

"Much of the demand came from jewellers wishing to make up stocks after weekend coin and jewellery sales, but there were also investors who took advantage of lower ounce prices to buy gold to swap with dollars" one dealer said.
The Turkish lira closed weaker at 100,500 to the dollar from 99,645 on Friday, passing the psychological 100,000 barrier for the first time.
Volume in the morning session was 636 kilos and shrank to 145 in the afternoon. 68.5 percent of total trade was in lira terms. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875
